Web sighs deeply. They think of leaving London, and how they still aren't sure it was the right choice. They think of joining the Golden Dawn. They think of burning down Jennerus Jack's shop. They think of lying to their friends, not leaving the Golden Dawn sooner. They think of sentencing Rah to death, then being too ashamed to even remember it. They remember choosing to look away as the Golden Dawn hurt Amara, letting her be controlled. They think of ruining her choices, how maybe they could have let her live. They think of forgetting Skitter, their own brother. They think of not telling Baeshra that the sub might be destroyed, causing her to lose so many of her possessions. They think of not telling Baeshra about the stone sooner. They think of ruining the colony's talk with the fishmother, and how they hurt Sandigill. They think of not pushing harder at the hag impersonating Wren, how maybe they could have saved the others sooner. They think of being careless the first time they raised the dead, corrupting the ground and making Wynne re-live being captured by hags. They think of how the hags returning to the ground made their curse last much longer. They think of dividing the town about necromancy, instead of bringing them together. They think of how they abandoned the puckwudgies for a time. They think of how still now, empty hill is ruling over them.

They think of Daysong's death, still feeling that he could have survived in physical form had he not used up a powerful spell on Web the week before. They think of Sandigill's death and how he might still be alive. They think of how it took them the death of a friend to actually be spurred into action. They think of how they ran when Baeshra died. How they still hate those woods. They think of how the Knights and Masons still argue, and that somehow they could have talked better to Florian. They think of everything with Lolth, and how that could have gone so much better in so many ways. They think of Hiram's death, and the fact that Solomon yet lives. They think of how they didn't handle their fear better, pushed others away. They think of all the times they could have helped baeshra and didn't, or helped the town and didn't. They think of how they still struggle so hard to control their primal urges, to be kind first, especially to strangers. They think of how it would still be so easy for them to be the self they fear. They count out their regrets one by one, breathing them in and out, hoping in some way to release them. They look up to the wardens, exhaling a long breath. “You all powerful enough. Will assume you got all that. Unless want Web to say out loud.”
